property_summary: For any admissible new owner, after setOwner(newOwner) the contract's owner getter returns newOwner; the mutant never updates owner, so it violates this for any newOwner different from the current owner.
For any address a passed by the current owner, calling setOwner(a) makes c.owner() equal a; the buggy version instead sets owner to msg.sender, so for any a != msg.sender the rule is violated.
For any address a, when the CURRENT owner calls setOwner(a), the contract's owner becomes exactly a; the mutant instead sets owner to msg.sender, so it violates this whenever a != msg.sender.
For any address a, calling setOwner(a) as the current owner sets owner to a; the buggy version instead sets owner to address(this), so owner != a for admissible inputs.

property_summary: For every caller and proposed owner, setOwner only changes owner when called by the current owner; the bug lets any non-owner caller overwrite owner, breaking the rule for some input.

property_summary: For any candidate address newOwner, a successful call to setOwner(newOwner) must leave c.owner() equal to newOwner; the mutant reverts on every call so owner is never updated and differs from newOwner.
For any caller who is the owner and any address, a successful setOwner call must return true; the mutant returns false, breaking this for every call.

property_summary: For any owner-supplied address, a successful call to setOwner returns true; the mutant omits the return so it returns false, violating this for every admissible call.

For any caller and any address, only the current owner can change the owner: a setOwner call from a non-owner must revert and leave c.owner() unchanged, but the buggy version lets any caller set owner.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): non-owner must not change owner

property_summary: For any caller and any new owner, setOwner succeeds if and only if the caller is the current owner (owner-only access control); the mutant inverts the require so the owner is rejected and some non-owner is accepted, breaking this rule.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): only the owner may set the owner

property_summary: For any admissible new owner address, calling setOwner(newOwner) as the current owner must set c.owner() exactly to that supplied address; the buggy version instead sets owner to msg.sender, so choosing a caller distinct from the argument breaks the rule.

After the owner transfers ownership to an address a, that address a itself gains owner privileges (a successful subsequent setOwner call from a), which the mutant breaks because it makes the old caller remain the owner.

For any caller equal to the current owner and any new owner address, a successful setOwner(a) must make c.owner() equal a; the mutant instead always stores address(0), so it violates the rule whenever a != address(0).
After any successful setOwner(a), the owner state must equal exactly a; the mutant instead overwrites owner with msg.sender, so for a!=owner the assertion c.owner()==a fails.

Whenever the current owner successfully calls setOwner(a), ownership moves exactly to the requested candidate a and nothing else — the mutant instead leaves owner set to the caller (msg.sender), so for any candidate a different from the caller the getter c.owner() returns the caller instead of a.

Ownership transfer takes effect: after the current owner successfully calls setOwner(a), the caller a itself acquires owner rights and can successfully perform a further setOwner; the mutant keeps control with the original caller so a's follow-up call reverts.

After the current owner transfers ownership to a distinct address, the original owner irrevocably loses owner rights (a follow-up setOwner by them must revert); the mutant keeps owner at the caller, so the follow-up call succeeds and breaks the rule.

After the current owner successfully calls setOwner(a), the owner state must become exactly a for every fuzzed candidate a; the mutant instead resets owner to msg.sender, so for any a != the calling owner the getter returns the caller instead of a.

For any caller and any address argument, a successful call by the current owner to setOwner must return true and set the owner to that argument; the mutant returns false (and skips the update) for every such call.
